consolidate-agent-memories.prompt: IMPORTANT: Before generating any report, read and follow ALL rules in ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/config/report-rules.md. Run memory consolidation. Working directory is ${SRC_ROOT}. Scan all sub-project memory dirs under ~/.claude/projects/Q--src*/memory/, compare against root memory at ~/.claude/projects/Q--src/memory/, copy new/updated files with ext_ prefix, remove duplicates, update MEMORY.md index (keep under 200 lines), run permission audit, root hygiene, stale file cleanup, and report template audit (scan all agent .md files under ~/.claude/agents/ and job configs under ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/config/jobs/*.json to verify HTML reports have VO subtitle, dark theme, Segoe UI, and are self-contained). If no meaningful work was done (no new memories found, no duplicates removed, no conflicts detected, and no stale files cleaned), do NOT generate an HTML report -- just output 'Memory consolidation: no changes found.' and exit. Only generate a full report when at least one memory was added, updated, deduplicated, or cleaned up. You MUST use the fixed template at ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/templates/mAuditor-memory-consolidation.html. Read the template file, then replace all {{PLACEHOLDER}} values with actual data. Replace {{VO_SUBTITLE}} with: Agent: Auditor | Job: consolidate-agent-memories | Start: <PST timestamp when job started> | Complete: <PST timestamp when report is generated>. Save the report to ${LOCAL_SKILLS}/session_management/memory-report-YYYYMMDD.html.
consolidate-agent-memories.description: Consolidates all sub-project memories into root, deduplicates, generates HTML report

teams-posting-audit.prompt: IMPORTANT: Read ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/config/report-rules.md Rule #8 and Rule #9 first. Run a Teams posting permission audit across all VO agent definitions and job configs. Scan: (1) All agent .md files in ~/.claude/agents/*.md -- search for keywords: Teams, channel, post, message, Graph API, graph.microsoft.com, chatMessage, @mention, agency copilot, send, notify. (2) All job configs in ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/config/jobs/*.json -- same keywords. (3) All runner scripts in ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/runner/ -- same keywords. For EACH match found, classify as: AUTHORIZED (mPoster agent job with explicit channel ID + fixed template in templates/), READ-ONLY (Graph API GET for data ingestion, not posting), DEPRECATED (has explicit deprecation note), or VIOLATION (unauthorized posting instruction -- any agent other than mPoster that posts to Teams, any posting without explicit channel ID, any posting without a fixed template). File a GitHub issue in jqxcode/virtual-office for each VIOLATION found, with the file path, line number, exact text, and recommended fix. If no violations found, output 'Teams posting audit: all clear.' and exit. Do NOT generate an HTML report for this job.
teams-posting-audit.description: Weekly audit of all agent defs and job configs for unauthorized Teams posting instructions

agent-brain-health-check.prompt: IMPORTANT: Before generating any report, read and follow ALL rules in ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/config/report-rules.md. Run the agent-brain-health-check job. First run: python ${REPO_PERSONAL}/agent-brain/scripts/health_check.py and capture all output. Then collect additional metrics: session archive coverage (sessions/ count vs ~/.claude/projects/ JSONL count), knowledge card freshness, last 10 git commits, audit log entries this week, entity counts. You MUST use the fixed template at ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/templates/mAuditor-agent-brain-health-check.html. Read the template file, then replace all {{PLACEHOLDER}} values with actual data. Replace {{VO_SUBTITLE}} with: Agent: Auditor | Job: agent-brain-health-check | Start: <PST timestamp when job started> | Complete: <PST timestamp when report is generated>. Use color thresholds: Green (sync <24h, digest <7d, 0 issues, all tests pass), Yellow (sync 24-48h, digest 7-14d, 1-2 issues), Red (sync >48h, digest >14d, 3+ issues, test failures). Save report to ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/output/mAuditor/agent-brain-health-YYYYMMDD.html (MUST be inside output/mAuditor/). Also save to ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/output/mAuditor/agent-brain-health-latest.html. Open the report in Edge after generation.
agent-brain-health-check.description: Weekly Agent Brain ecosystem health check with HTML dashboard report

schedule-health-check.prompt:
Run the schedule-health-check job. This is a guard that catches scheduled VO jobs that have silently stopped running (e.g. an agent rename that left Windows Scheduled Tasks launching dead agent names). Working directory is ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office. Two parts:

PART 1 -- task/config reconciliation. Run: pwsh -File ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/runner/Verify-Schedules.ps1 and capture its full stdout and exit code. Exit 0 = PASS (live VO-* agent-job tasks fully reconciled with config/schedules.json). Non-zero = FAIL (dead-agent tasks, missing tasks, or orphan tasks). Include the PASS/FAIL verdict and the detail of any flagged task in your report.

PART 2 -- missed-run detection from events. Read config/schedules.json. For EACH schedule entry whose cron runs on weekdays -- that is, the day-of-week field (5th field) is '*' (daily) OR a range/list that includes any of Mon-Fri such as '1-5' -- determine whether that agent+job actually started recently. IMPORTANT: do NOT trust Windows Task Scheduler LastTaskResult -- it reports 0 (success) even when the job never ran, because the Run-Hidden.vbs launcher always exits clean. The ONLY reliable signal is state/events.jsonl. Read state/events.jsonl (each line is JSON with fields agent, job, event, timestamp; event 'started' marks an actual run start). For each weekday-scheduled agent+job, assert that at least one event with event=='started' for that exact agent AND job appears with a timestamp within the last ~26 hours (use 26h to tolerate clock skew and a job that runs once daily). Today is a weekday only when relevant -- if you run on a Monday, jobs whose cron is strictly weekday-only ('1-5') legitimately did not run over the weekend, so for a Monday run compare against the most recent weekday; for a normal weekday run a 26h window is correct. Compute timestamps programmatically with python or pwsh -- never compute day-of-week by hand.

List every weekday-scheduled job that SHOULD have run in the window but has NO matching 'started' event -- these are the silently-dead jobs. For each, show agent, job, cron, and the timestamp of its most recent 'started' event (or 'never') so the operator can see how long it has been dead.

OUTPUT: a concise plain-text report (no HTML). Structure: (1) Verify-Schedules result line (PASS/FAIL + counts), (2) a 'Missed runs' section listing any silently-dead weekday jobs with their last-seen timestamp, (3) a one-line verdict. If Verify-Schedules PASSED and every weekday-scheduled job has a 'started' event within the window, state clearly: 'Schedule health: all clear -- N weekday jobs checked, all ran within 26h, tasks reconciled.' and exit. Only escalate (list problems prominently) when something is actually wrong. Do NOT generate an HTML report for this job. Do NOT register, unregister, or modify any scheduled task -- this job is read-only diagnostics.
schedule-health-check.description: Daily guard: reconcile live scheduled tasks vs config (Verify-Schedules) and flag any weekday-scheduled job with no 'started' event in events.jsonl within ~26h

brain-weekly-maintenance.prompt: Run the brain-weekly-maintenance job. Working directory is ${REPO_PERSONAL}/agent-brain. Execute the canonical, idempotent weekly maintenance pipeline that chains archive -> compile -> compress -> push: run `python ${REPO_PERSONAL}/agent-brain/scripts/weekly_brain_maintenance.py` and capture its full stdout and exit code. The script archives completed sessions, compiles knowledge cards, compresses/prunes stale memories, and pushes the brain repo. Do NOT run the individual steps by hand -- the single script is the supported entry point and is safe to re-run. If the script exits non-zero, report the failing step and its output; do not attempt manual recovery. OUTPUT: a concise plain-text summary of each step's result and a one-line verdict. Do NOT generate an HTML report for this job.
brain-weekly-maintenance.description: Weekly brain maintenance: archive sessions, compile knowledge, compress, push (Sunday 10pm) via agent-brain/scripts/weekly_brain_maintenance.py
